newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse high-caps, turnover on the rise.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse high-caps, turnover on the rise.

text.p: Bucharest bourse first-tier stocks stayed in the limelight on Tuesday, seeing their closing prices drift higher in heavy trading.

Share prices on the second tier were mixed, but several notable rises in average quotes, along with price jolts on the first tier, sent two independent indices to year highs and above their starting bases.

Two special trades in high-cap Azomures fertiliser maker and the return to the market after suspension of first-tier pharmaceuticals company Antibiotice pushed turnover 1.4 billion lei higher to 8.29 billion.
"The two special deals were struck with foreign investors," a Bucharest broker said.
The trades -- large deals struck outside the market and reported to the exchange later -- involved a total 400,000 Azomures shares worth an overall 1.4 billion lei.
Azomures closed 100 lei firmer at 3,500 and Antibiotice ended at 6,450 lei, up from 4,600 before suspension.
The other pharmaceutical, Terapia, closed 1,800 lei higher at 7,400 and chemical plant Oltchim ended the day 250 lei stronger at 2,800.
Buying interest was thin in stocks on the second tier, where eight companies had no trade and six were suspended.
Several second-tier stocks rose heavily in low supply, with average prices climbing to up to 50 percent in some cases.

The VAB and the BIG unofficial indices rose by 9.9 and 10.12 percent respectively from the previous session to 1,041 and 1,020.44 points. Their base is 1,000 points. The BIG first-tier index jumped by 12.63 percent to 3,690.73 points.
